newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Lonrho's Bock steps down as chief executive.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Lonrho's Bock steps down as chief executive.

text.p: German financier Dieter Bock, the man who deposed Tiny Rowland in a fierce boardroom battle 18 months ago, announced on Tuesday he would be stepping down as chief executive of the Lonrho conglomerate .
Tiny Rowland, a colourful business tycoon who has kept up a public feud with Bock, ran the company for 34 years until March 1995. His bitter scuffles with Bock over Lonrho strategy are legendary.

Bock, who will remain as non-executive deputy chairman, has seen through the demerger of the company into three separate divisions and declared his ambition to become chief executive of Lonrho's trading business earlier this year.
The company is being broken up into three sectors -- mining, trading and hotels.
Bock said his aim of running the trading business, which mainly involves dealing in car dealerships and agricultural commodities, "will be better pursued from a non-executive position."
Bock will be succeeded by deputy managing director Nicholas Morrell.
The company also expected to announce shortly the "successful sale of Metropole and Princess Hotels", Bock said.
Lonrho intends to focus purely on its mining business once the other divisions are hived off.
Separately on Tuesday, Anglo-American, the South African mining company said it was buying a further 18.3 percent stake in Lonrho from Bock's Laerstate BV.
